topic.title: Why Elon Musk can't just sell his shares and give the money away

title: Why Elon Musk doesn't just sell and give it away 💸
description:
Can Elon Musk just sell his shares and give the cash away?
Over a few weeks in late 2021 he sold nearly $14B of Tesla; he said he'd pay over $11B in tax that year, on sales and options together.
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Should he give shares or cash? Comment

lines.text: You think Musk just sells and gives it away? Watch.
His money isn't cash in a bank. It's mostly Tesla shares.
In one stretch of a few weeks, he sold nearly $14B of Tesla.
That year he said he'd pay over $11B in tax, on sales and options together.
So what if he sold everything?
Sell an illustrative $100.00B at the top US rate, 23.8%.
Before a cent is given, $23.80B goes to tax.
The twist? Give the shares themselves, and the US charges no capital gains tax on them.
That's the catch: selling first shrinks the gift by $23.80B.
Still think he'd just sell and hand it all out?

Giving appreciated shares to charity incurs no capital-gains tax, which is correct. Title, payoff and loop now claim only that selling first costs tax. 'Illustrative $100B' as the verify list requires. Disclaimer present. Small notes: fact3 ($937B) is still in facts but used nowhere, so drop it (and its wrong Reuters credit; the figure is Bloomberg's). The 23.8% bill assumes a near-zero cost basis, which is reasonable for a founder.

payoff + title: 'That's why he can't just give it away' / 'Elon Musk can't just give it away' is false and the numbers don't support it. He can donate shares directly with no capital-gains tax (he gave about $5.7B of Tesla shares to charity in Nov 2021), and even the video's own sale leaves 76.2% to give. The most the story shows is that selling first costs tax. Reword title, payoff and loop to 'can't just SELL and give the cash away without losing a big chunk', or mention giving shares directly.

sold + tax beats: 'nearly $14B of Tesla... And the bill? He said he'd pay over $11B in tax' presents the $11B as the bill on the $14B sale (it reads as about 79%). Most of the tax came from exercising about 15M options taxed as income (Gulf News, Deseret, Bloomberg Tax). The topic's verify list says never present the $11B as a rate on the $14B. Separate them, e.g. say the tax 'mostly came from exercising options', or drop 'And the bill?'.
sold beat: 'He did sell once' is false. Musk sold Tesla stock again in 2022 (about $23B across April, August and Nov-Dec, around the Twitter deal). Say 'In late 2021 he sold...' instead.

turn + payoff: 'while he sold, Tesla's value slid... to $937B' followed by 'his billions shrink before he gives them' credits the drop to his selling. The sources only say the value slid after the poll/tweet. Keep it as timing only, with no causal payoff.

fact3 ($937B) is not on the cited Reuters/Yahoo page (it says 'about $1 trillion'). Confirmed by search instead: Accounting Today (Bloomberg News, 21 Dec 2021: 'slid back below the $1 trillion mark to $937 billion') and Deseret News (20 Dec 2021). Credit it to Bloomberg, not Reuters. fact1 ($11B) and fact2 (nearly $14B, 'last few weeks') are confirmed on the Reuters page. 23.8% (20% LTCG + 3.8% NIIT, federal) is correct.
